subject: Vocabulary
description: Common Greek/Latin prefixes — anti, ante, ad, con, dis, mis, sub, super, trans

options.option_text: Against, opposite of (like anti-)
Before, prior to (Latin origin)
After, following (like post-)
Beneath, under (like sub-)

questions.explanation: ANTE- = before. Examples: ANTECHAMBER (room before main chamber), ANTEDATE (before a date), ANTEROOM, ANTEBELLUM (pre-war). DON'T confuse with ANTI- (against): antithesis, antibody, antigravity. POST- = after. SUB- = under. ANTE comes from Latin; ANTI from Greek.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Many or much (like multi-)
Wrongly, badly, or in error
Half, partial (like semi-)
Together with (like co-)

questions.explanation: MIS- = wrongly, badly. Examples: MISUNDERSTAND (understand wrongly), MISUSE, MISCALCULATE, MISBEHAVE, MISPRONOUNCE. Old English origin. Distractors are different prefixes: MULTI- (many), SEMI- (half), CO-/COM-/CON- (together).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Above, beyond (like super-)
Across, through, beyond a boundary
Beneath, under (like sub-)
Many, multiple (like multi-)

questions.explanation: TRANS- = across, through, beyond. Latin origin. Examples: TRANSPORT (carry across), TRANSCONTINENTAL (across a continent), TRANSFER, TRANSPLANT, TRANSPARENT (light passes through), TRANSLATE (carry meaning across languages). SUPER- = above. SUB- = under. MULTI- = many.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The prefix DIS- (as in 'disagree', 'dishonest') typically means:

options.option_text: Two or twice (like bi-)
Not, opposite of, or apart from
Down, below (like sub-)
Half, partial (like semi-)

questions.explanation: DIS- = not, opposite of, or apart. Examples: DISAGREE, DISHONEST, DISCOURAGE, DISCONNECT, DISLIKE, DISAPPEAR. Latin origin. Same family: UN- (English; unhappy, undo), IN-/IM- (Latin; incomplete, impossible), NON- (nonexistent). Distractor 1 BI- (twice). Distractor 3 SUB- (under). Distractor 4 SEMI- (half).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Inside, internal (like the prefix intra-)
Around, encompassing (Latin origin)
Two or double (like the prefix bi-)
Through or across (like the prefix trans-)

questions.explanation: CIRCUM- = around. Latin 'circum' (around). Examples: CIRCUMNAVIGATE (sail around), CIRCUMFERENCE (boundary around a circle), CIRCUMSPECT (literally 'looking around' → cautious), CIRCUMVENT (go around an obstacle), CIRCUMSCRIBE (draw a line around → limit). Same root as 'circle'. Distractor 1 INTRA-. Distractor 3 BI-. Distractor 4 TRANS-.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Below the normal level (like prefix hypo-)
Above the normal level, excessive level
Equal to a baseline (like prefix equi-)
Of the self or own (like the prefix auto-)

questions.explanation: HYPER- = above, excessive. Greek origin. Examples: HYPERTENSION (high BP), HYPERACTIVE, HYPERSONIC (>5× speed of sound), HYPERBOLE (extreme exaggeration). DISTINGUISHED from HYPO- = below, deficient: HYPOTENSION (low BP), HYPOTHERMIA, HYPOTHESIS. Both Greek; one letter difference makes them opposite. Distractor 3 EQUI-. Distractor 4 AUTO-.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Before, prior to (like pre-)
After, behind, following in time
Away from, outside (like ex-)
Within, inside (like intra-)

questions.explanation: POST- = after. Latin origin. Examples: POSTPONE (delay to a later time), POSTWAR (after the war), POST-MORTEM (after death; medical examination), POSTGRADUATE, POSTSCRIPT. Antonym prefix: PRE- = before. Distractor 1 PRE-. Distractor 3 EX-. Distractor 4 INTRA-/IN-.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The prefix SUB- appears in 'submarine', 'substandard', and 'subordinate'. What common meaning does it carry across all three words?

options.option_text: above and beyond the usual standard
under, below, or of lesser rank
between two or more separate things
across or through an existing barrier

questions.explanation: SUB- derives from Latin 'sub' meaning 'under' or 'below.' Submarine = under the sea; substandard = below standard; subordinate = under in rank. Option A describes SUPER- or EXTRA-, not SUB-.

questions.stem: Which of the following words contains a prefix meaning 'back to a former state' or 'once again'?

options.option_text: PRELUDE — an introductory musical composition
MISGUIDE — to lead someone in a wrong direction
REVIVE — to bring something back to life or use
SUBVERT — to undermine a system from within

questions.explanation: RE- in REVIVE comes from Latin 're' meaning 'again' or 'back.' REVIVE = to live again. PRE- means 'before', MIS- means 'wrongly', and SUB- means 'under' — none carry the sense of repetition or return.

questions.stem: The prefix RETRO- in 'retrograde', 'retrofit', and 'retrospective' consistently conveys which meaning?

options.option_text: moving forward or advancing to a new stage
moving backward or directed toward the past
happening at the same time in two places
occurring in cycles or at regular intervals

questions.explanation: RETRO- is Latin for 'backward' or 'behind.' Retrograde = moving backward; retrofit = adapt an old design; retrospective = looking back in time. Option A describes PRO- or FORE-, which mean forward or in advance.

questions.stem: A medical report states a patient's skin absorbs 'INFRA-red radiation.' The prefix INFRA- as used here means:

options.option_text: above the visible range of human perception
within the exact midpoint of the spectrum
below or beneath a given threshold or range
spanning across the full electromagnetic band

questions.explanation: INFRA- (Latin 'infra') means 'below.' Infrared = below red on the visible light spectrum. Students frequently confuse it with ULTRA- (beyond/above), since both describe invisible radiation — but ULTRA- means beyond the upper bound, INFRA- below the lower.

questions.stem: The prefix OMNI- in 'omnivore', 'omnipotent', and 'omniscient' carries which core Latin meaning?

options.option_text: many or several, present in multiple forms
all or every, without any limitation whatsoever
greatly exceeding the usual or expected level
one or single, completely undivided in nature

questions.explanation: OMNI- comes from Latin 'omnis' meaning 'all.' Omnivore = eats all food types; omnipotent = all-powerful; omniscient = all-knowing. The most tempting distractor is POLY- (many/several), but POLY- implies plurality, not totality — an important distinction examiners exploit.

questions.stem: The words 'anarchy', 'anemia', 'anomaly', and 'analogy' all begin with 'AN-'. In which word does AN- NOT carry the Greek meaning of 'without' or 'not'?

options.option_text: ANARCHY — absence of any governing authority
ANEMIA — deficiency in red blood cell count
ANALOGY — comparison drawn on shared similarity
ANOMALY — departure from what is considered normal

questions.explanation: ANALOGY derives from Greek ANA- (according to / proportionate) + LOGOS (reason), NOT from A-/AN- (without). By contrast: ANARCHY = AN- (without) + ARCHOS (rule); ANEMIA = AN- (without) + HAEMA (blood); ANOMALY = AN- (without) + HOMALOS (even/regular). This AN-/ANA- trap is a classic examiner move.

questions.stem: The prefix PARA- has two distinct etymological senses in English. In 'paranormal' it comes from Greek meaning 'beyond,' while in 'parachute' it derives from Italian 'parare' with a different sense. Which pairing correctly identifies both?

options.option_text: beside or beyond (paranormal) and protection from (parachute)
below or under (paranormal) and movement toward (parachute)
against or opposing (paranormal) and half of (parachute)
across or through (paranormal) and false or imitation (parachute)

questions.explanation: Greek PARA- means 'beside/beyond': paranormal = beyond normal; parallel = beside each other. In 'parachute', PARA- is Italian/French from 'parare' = 'to guard against' + 'chute' (fall), giving 'protection from a fall.' Option C confuses PARA- with ANTI- (against), and Option D with PSEUDO- (false/imitation).
